primary_followup.rationale: Primary sponsor describes closing recruitment and completing existing patients while prioritising distinct AB-1009. Treat as superseded under the user-defined molecule rule; this is a portfolio decision, not demonstrated lack of efficacy. March formal discontinuation is additionally reported by secondary sources; inaccessible primary March deck is not claimed as read.
Phase II was terminated following unblinding. That establishes a stopped trial, not independently verified permanent abandonment of the molecule in SCD.
MPS I studies completed. Acquisition of ArmaGen and different JCR successors do not establish the disposition of this specific molecule. Vendor abandonment remains uncorroborated.
MPS II study completed with six participants. No retrieved primary statement establishes permanent abandonment or a current registration programme for this molecule.

Protalix stopped further CF development in 2019; subsequent SarcoMed licence and sarcoidosis work do not establish current CF development. Continuing original CF rights/pathway unresolved; vendor active is not independently validated.
NewcelX 2026 filing retains AstroRx as an ALS clinical-stage platform-validation asset. Active here means retained programme, not independently verified new patient dosing or pivotal commitment.
Licensor 2026 filing retains EL22/BLS-M22 DMD development. Obesity development is a separate indication. Active means retained DMD programme; no new DMD dosing established in this review.
BioMarin disclosed a clinical hold and requested additional preclinical work; registry retains active-not-recruiting status. Hold is not permanent failure and follow-up is not resumed development.
Huntington study terminated for recruitment problems. No primary evidence retrieved of definitive molecule-level abandonment.
Completed early studies and later bronchiectasis work do not establish current CF advancement or permanent CF abandonment. Keep original indication scope.
FALCON combination study completed; weak combination results and transfer to AbbVie alone do not prove definitive CF molecule abandonment. Do not confuse with navocaftor/GLPG3067.
ADPKD trial termination for efficacy is not a CF outcome. CF trials completed; original CF programme disposition not independently resolved.

Sponsor terminated long-term study for product-development prioritisation and withdrew further UCD study. Classify exit from the selected metabolic programme; mixed UCD/Crigler-Najjar entry still requires pair-level separation. Not an efficacy-failure claim.

Sponsor 2026 reports clinical DMD programme and follow-up in treated children. Fourth participant died after ARDS; other three remain in follow-up. Active-follow-up classification is not evidence of resumed recruitment or favourable safety.

Two pulmonary hypertension trials terminated by sponsor decision. No retrieved primary evidence establishes whether programme permanently abandoned or replaced by HS235; do not treat a successor's activity as rescue.
Registry says suspended because of drug shortage, with possible resumption and continuing survival follow-up. This contradicts treating the available primary record as definitive permanent failure.
Sponsor February 2025 reports completed Phase IIa work and continuing development of Huntington asset. Retained programme, not independently established ongoing dosing.
PAH trial terminated with seven participants; other studies completed. No retrieved primary statement settles permanent molecule-level exit.

selected_indications: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (early study included PH2)

primary_followup.rationale: Completed SCD Phase I study with 21 participants; current development fate not independently established.
Retrospectively registered healthy-volunteer study completed in 2023. No retrieved primary evidence of a current ALS patient programme; vendor Phase I alone is insufficient.

Gemma registry retains GM1 clinical follow-up. Passage filing reports unpaid transfer instalment; financing uncertainty does not by itself prove abandonment. Active-follow-up only, not verified new dosing.
Pfizer August 2023 pipeline explicitly lists discontinuation. Later registry completion/update does not reverse the sponsor's development decision.
QR-313 trial terminated for low enrolment; transfer to Wings/Phoenicis does not establish subsequent permanent abandonment. Current original-indication fate unresolved.

Ultragenyx stopped US development after Phase III failure, but aceneuramic acid subsequently received Japanese approval. Do not call the molecule globally failed or count foreign approval as FDA success; future FDA path remains unknown.
Sponsor describes current stroke development and historical SCD work. Activity in stroke does not establish active SCD development or a definitive SCD exit.

Sanofi reports discontinuation in rare renal disease; the panel maps the healthy-volunteer study to PNH. Neither that cross-indication exit nor completion of healthy-volunteer dosing establishes the original PNH programme's terminal outcome. Pair mapping needs verification.
Botanical SCD-101 record is stale/unknown. A search match to protocol 6058-SCD-101 is pociredir, a different molecule, and is explicitly rejected as status evidence.
Completed healthy-volunteer study does not establish permanent HAE programme abandonment or current advancement.
Divesiran is advancing in polycythemia vera; original beta-thalassemia/MDS trial completed. Later indication activity cannot resolve the original thalassemia programme.
Roche July 2024 materials identify portfolio termination/removal. Continued safety follow-up in registry does not make the development programme active.

evidence.note: 2019 Specials-license first treated child predates 2020 formal study. Same technology/procedures per sponsor; formal trial clock shown separately in source.
Sponsor first-dose May 2019 release overrides later formal registry start. Academic trial continues despite sponsor exit; distinct from LYS-GM101/PBGM01.
Sponsor confirms first treated child in Brazil by Dec20 2022; year interval rather than release date as dosing day. Vendor identifies Tern continuation.
First dosing March2022; current registry suspended/company-strategy stop despite Gemma transfer and vendor PhaseII. Restart versus terminal exit unresolved; not automatically active or failed.
Registry actual start lower bound, treated-patient data establish exposure2021. Rights returned to Queens2024; ongoing clinical follow-up does not prove new dosing/commercial advancement.
Bound between IND clearance and180days before Aug30 2022 data release. Jan28 2025 sponsor discontinuation overrides vendor PhaseII. Exact first-dose date unknown.

Treatment confirmed by Feb2024;2021 clinical-start announcement is NOT dosing. Feb2026 license termination, but potential academic continuation uncertain. Broad date interval; exclude in stronger-entry sensitivity.

evidence.rationale: CTIS reports actual trial start 20 March 2018, recruitment ending November 2020, and global trial end 2 October 2025. Treated cohort reported by April 2021. Registry start is not proven first dose; use conservative interval, exclude in stronger-entry sensitivity. Completion does not establish permanent failure or advancement.

Cystinosis autologous HSC gene therapy first treated October 2019. Original trial completed; long-term follow-up continues. Novartis DFT383 development provides a continuation lead, but exact manufacturing continuity should be checked before counting new trial as identical construct. Broad rare tier only: systemic cystinosis, not CNS-targeted.
